bug_semantics: The kernel's CheckAuth middleware grants RoleAdministrator to any request whose RemoteAddr is loopback for a fixed set of URIs — /assets/, /history/assets/, /export/, /api/system/exit, /api/system/getNetwork, /api/system/getWorkspaceInfo (plus SiYuanAccessAuthCodeBypass when no access-auth code is set). These localhost passthroughs sit outside the access-auth-code gate, so they apply even when a lock-screen password is configured. The fixed-port reverse proxy (kernel/server/proxy/fixedport.go) forwards browser requests to the kernel over loopback WITHOUT injecting any auth token and without trusted-proxy handling, so a forwarded request reaches the kernel with RemoteAddr = 127.0.0.1 and is treated as a local administrator request — authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290): a remote attacker hitting the fixed-port proxy gains admin endpoints (/api/system/exit kills the kernel, getWorkspaceInfo leaks paths, /assets/ + /export/ read arbitrary content).
flaw_origin: Commit ed3a6fcb9ab5403bbcc60db78b4f72ddc765668e ("鉴权页关闭窗口失效" [#5149], 2022-06-11, author+committer Liang Ding <d@b3log.org>) generalized an existing narrow /assets/-only localhost passthrough (introduced with CheckAuth in the initial open-source drop f40ed985e10b) into a multi-endpoint admin bypass keyed purely on `strings.HasPrefix(c.Request.RemoteAddr, "127.0.0.1")` — the RemoteAddr-trust design that persists through v3.7.2 and is the flaw the advisory names. Later commits only appended endpoints to the same trusted-RemoteAddr pattern (cb016aac14f0 2023-11-21 auth rework kept it; 3c755b1864f5 2023-11-24 added getNetwork; 691290a7be30 2024-11-29 added getWorkspaceInfo; ff4d215f78a8 2025-08-28 added publish proxy), and the fixed-port proxy shipped with no token/forwarded-header handling. Parent 21f1f48a5 has the /assets/-only variant; the BIC is where the bypass became RemoteAddr-keyed admin access for control endpoints (/api/system/exit), which parent lacks.
